text:
simon: Heads up — after the GPU-operator/device-plugin rollout (image v0.12.3) we are seeing a wave of GPU pod evictions in prod-us-west-2 starting ~09:10 UTC. Pods report allocation failures even though drivers appear present on nodes.

maya: saw this too, ~50 pods failed in the last 20m. kubelet logs show a bunch of liveness probe backoffs for device-plugin: 

simon: pasted the short grep of kubelet: `May 06 09:11:22 ip-10-0-2-31 kubelet[...]: liveness probe failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport is closing"`

jordana: node `gpu-frontend-12` shows `nvidia-smi` OK: driver 525.85.12, nodesight up. But the pod error is `FailedScheduling: 0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` even though `kubectl describe node` shows allocatable GPUs.

arjun: also saw NCCL errors on a few training jobs earlier: `ncclSystemError` before they got evicted. My read: device-plugin is flapping under probe stress, kube-scheduler momentarily thinks GPUs unavailable and evicts.

maya: deploy-bot reported device-plugin restarted ~3x/min on some nodes — looks like probe throttle/regression in v0.12.3. ops-bot added taints `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule` on two nodes (health checks).

simon: quick debug outputs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs dp-xxxxx`: shows repeated registration and unregistering with driver-manager: `RegisterDevices() failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to open /dev/nvidia0: no such file or directory` even though `ls /dev | grep nvidia` shows devices present. Suspect probe ordering race with driver plugin init.

jordana: rolling back device-plugin to v0.12.2 on a small canary fixed allocation on those nodes — pods started scheduling again. Canary nodes have plugin image digest `sha256:xxx`.

arjun: for mitigation we should: 1) pin device-plugin image to v0.12.2 on remaining clusters, 2) pause full rollout, 3) schedule node drains slowly to recover backlog and avoid mass eviction. Also we may want to increase kubelet probe timeout.

maya: agree. cost note: this caused about ~3h of queued jobs and some training jobs retried on on-demand instances -> extra $2.6k estimated for the wave in us-west-2 (billing spike). Flagging finance?

simon: filed a ticket with GPU-operator maintainers with logs and probe traces. Link: https://github.com/redwood/gpu-operator/issues/412 (internal fork). They asked for driver-manager logs and kernel dmesg.

arjun: next steps: (a) pause rollout in other regions, (b) coordinate driver restarts on canaries to ensure probe sequence, (c) add temporary kubelet flag to relax device-plugin liveness (or bump probe initialDelaySeconds), (d) capacity: spin up 8 spare nodes in us-west-2 to reduce scheduling pressure.

jordana: I'm starting the pin/rollback now for all control planes in us-west-2. Will post progress.

maya: FYI I'm opening a cost-impact ticket and marking it P1 for us-west-2 SLA review.

deploy-bot: rollout status — cluster: prod-us-west-2: paused by jordana at 09:34 UTC.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-20260506-87 (label: gpu-op-probe-throttle). Assigned to eng-infra oncall.

simon: thanks — will collect driver-manager + dmesg from 3 affected nodes and attach to the GitHub issue. If anyone sees a different pattern (kernel module unload, DKMS messages), ping here.
